---
title: "Contributing and releases"
description: "How to report a problem, propose a change across the repository and its forks, keep the docs in step, and make a release."
---

## Report a problem {#issues}

Open an issue at [github.com/0xMuluh/omicsbase/issues](https://github.com/0xMuluh/omicsbase/issues). Every page of these docs also has a "Report an issue" link.

A good issue is short:

1. What you did.
2. What you expected.
3. What happened instead, with the exact error text.
4. Where: omicsbase.utu.fi or a local install, and which version.

Keep problems in separate issues, one each.

## Branches {#branches}

1. Start from the current `main` of the omicsbase repository.
2. Name the branch after the kind of change: `feat/…` for a feature, `fix/…` for a bug fix, `docs/…` for docs only, `chore/…` for upkeep. For example `fix/install-progress-memory-arm`.

### Changes in a fork {#fork-branches}

If your change touches `librechat/` or `openhands/`, it needs two pull requests: one in the fork, one in the omicsbase repository.

1. Inside the submodule, start from the fork's working branch:

   | Submodule | Start from |
   | --- | --- |
   | `librechat/` | `chore/librechat-upstream-20261021` |
   | `openhands/` | `chore/openhands-v1.41.0` |

2. Use the same branch name in the fork and in the omicsbase repository, so the pair is easy to find.
3. Open the fork's pull request against that working branch.
4. After it is merged, check out the merge commit inside the submodule.
5. Commit the new submodule pointer in the omicsbase repository and open that pull request. Name the fork pull request in its description.

## Pull requests {#prs}

Keep the description short: what changed and why, in a few lines. The template asks one question: does this change what users or self-hosters see?

### Update the docs in the same pull request {#docs-rule}

If your change alters what users or self-hosters see, update the docs page in the same pull request. Tick the box in the template, or say that no page is affected.

For a change in a fork, the docs live in the omicsbase repository. Put the docs change in the omicsbase pull request that moves the submodule pointer, and link the two.

### The docs check {#docs-ci}

The workflow `.github/workflows/docs.yml` runs on every pull request that touches `docs/`, `scripts/build_changelog.sh` or the workflow itself. It:

1. Writes the changelog from the GitHub releases.
2. Renders the site with Quarto 1.11 and the `publish` profile.
3. Checks that `llms.txt` was written.
4. Checks every link between the site's own pages, with the link checker lychee.

The pull request fails on a render error or a broken link. The same check runs on pushes to `main`. A weekly run, and a manual run, also check links to other sites.

To catch problems before you push, preview the site locally; see [Preview these docs](dev-loop.qmd#docs).

### The engine image check {#engine-ci}

The workflow `.github/workflows/engine-image.yml` runs on every pull request that touches `engine/`. It copies `knowledge.db` from a published engine image with `scripts/fetch_knowledge_db.py`, builds the engine image, runs each file in `engine/tests` inside it, and loads a few R packages as a random user in group 0, as on LUMI-K. It also extracts the help pages, vignettes and exports of the image's R packages with `scripts/build_package_knowledge.py` and uploads them as the `package-knowledge` artifact; when the R packages change, commit its two files to `engine/knowledge/`. It pushes nothing. The run takes about 35 minutes.

## Make a release {#release}

A release is three things with the same version name, for example `2026.11.22`:

- the images, pushed to `ghcr.io/0xmuluh/omicsbase-librechat`, `omicsbase-engine` and `omicsbase-reports` with that tag and with `latest`;
- a Git tag on the released commit of `main`;
- a GitHub release with notes generated from the merged pull requests.

Local installs take their images by this name: `OMICSBASE_VERSION` in their `.env` is `latest` unless set to a version.

### 1. Build the images {#release-build}

1. Check out the commit of `main` you want to release, with its submodules:

   ```bash
   git switch --detach <sha>
   git submodule update --init --recursive
   ```

2. Build the three images, as in [Build the images](dev-loop.qmd#from-source-build) and [Run the local install with your own images](dev-loop.qmd#own-images):

   ```bash
   python3 scripts/build_engine.py --context default
   python3 scripts/build_openhands.py --context default
   python3 scripts/build_librechat.py --context default
   ```

3. Test them in a local install with `OMICSBASE_VERSION=dev`, as in [Run the local install with your own images](dev-loop.qmd#own-images).

### 2. Push the images {#release-push}

1. Sign in to the GitHub container registry with a token that has `write:packages`:

   ```bash
   docker login ghcr.io
   ```

2. Tag and push each image with the version and with `latest`. For the engine:

   ```bash
   docker tag omicsbase-engine:dev ghcr.io/0xmuluh/omicsbase-engine:<version>
   docker tag omicsbase-engine:dev ghcr.io/0xmuluh/omicsbase-engine:latest
   docker push ghcr.io/0xmuluh/omicsbase-engine:<version>
   docker push ghcr.io/0xmuluh/omicsbase-engine:latest
   ```

3. Do the same for `omicsbase-openhands:dev` as `ghcr.io/0xmuluh/omicsbase-reports`, and for `omicsbase-librechat:<commit>` as `ghcr.io/0xmuluh/omicsbase-librechat`.

### 3. Tag and publish the release {#release-tag}

1. Tag the released commit and push the tag:

   ```bash
   git tag <version> <sha>
   git push origin <version>
   ```

2. Create the GitHub release, with notes generated from the merged pull requests:

   ```bash
   gh release create <version> --target <sha> --generate-notes
   ```

   `gh` prints the address of the new release.

### 4. Publish the docs {#release-docs}

1. Publish the docs for this version:

   ```bash
   OMICSBASE_VM=<user>@<host> scripts/publish_docs.sh <version>
   ```

   It ends with:

   ```text
   Published: https://omicsbase.utu.fi/docs/ and /docs/<version>/
   ```

The script first rebuilds `docs/changelog.qmd` from the GitHub releases (`scripts/build_changelog.sh`), so the new release appears on the [Changelog](../changelog.qmd). It then copies the site to `/docs/` and keeps a copy at `/docs/<version>/`. See [Publish the docs](production.qmd#docs) for what it needs.

### The Reports image for Roihu and own computers {#release-roihu-image}

Roihu jobs and attached computers use a different image, built from `deployment/roihu/Dockerfile`. It is published to `ghcr.io/0xmuluh/omicsbase-reports` under its own tags, such as `v1.41.0-roihu4`. Installs choose it with `ROIHU_IMAGE_TAG`. See [Reports on Roihu](production.qmd#roihu) for how to build and roll it out.

## Licence {#licence}

- Original OmicsBase code is under the [MIT licence](https://github.com/0xMuluh/omicsbase/blob/main/LICENSE).
- LibreChat's MIT licence is kept in `licenses/LIBRECHAT-LICENSE`.
- OpenHands' notices are kept in `licenses/OPENHANDS-LICENSE`.
- The vendored Prism syntax highlighter's licence is kept in `licenses/PRISM-LICENSE`.
- The books in the knowledge index keep their own licences. They are listed in `knowledge/ATTRIBUTION.md` and are not covered by the MIT licence.

`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` lists the third-party code. Dependencies installed by the upstream projects keep their own licences.
